source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲכִ֣י יֶשׁ־ע֔וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר נוֹתַ֖ר לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה עִמּוֹ֙ חֶ֔סֶד בַּעֲב֖וּר יְהוֹנָתָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, [is it] that there is still [one] who is left of [the] house of Saul, and I will do with him steadfast love for [the] sake of Jonathan?

en.L: And David said, "Is there still anyone who is left of the house of Saul, that I may deal [in] steadfast love with him for the sake of Jonathan?"
en.B: David asked, "Is there anyone still left from the house of Saul, so that I can show him faithful love for Jonathan's sake?"
en.R: One day David asked, "Is anyone from Saul's family still alive? If so, I want to show him faithful love because of my friend Jonathan."

fr.L: Et David dit : « Y a-t-il encore quelqu’un qui reste de la maison de Saül, pour que j’agisse envers lui avec amour loyal à cause de Jonathan ? »
fr.B: David demanda : « Reste-t-il encore quelqu’un de la maison de Saül, pour que je lui montre un amour fidèle à cause de Jonathan ? »
fr.R: Un jour, David a demandé : « Est-ce qu’il y a encore quelqu’un de la famille de Saül qui soit en vie ? Si c’est le cas, je veux lui montrer un amour fidèle à cause de mon ami Jonathan. »

decisions.choice: faithful love for Jonathan's sake: David keeps the promise he made to Jonathan
decisions.reason: Jonathan had asked David never to cut off his steadfast love from his family, even when Yahweh had removed all David's enemies, and the two had bound themselves by an oath before Yahweh (1 Samuel 20:14-17, 42). With his kingdom now secure (8:1-15), David looks for a way to keep that oath.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal kindness owed within a bond
decisions.reason: The word means more than a kind feeling. It is the loyalty and generous care that a covenant or a close tie calls for, given freely and kept over time. It returns in verses 3 and 7 and shapes the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: the house of Saul: Saul's family and descendants
decisions.reason: "House" means a family line. A new ruling house often wiped out the old king's descendants so that none could claim the throne (1 Kings 15:29; 16:11); David instead searches for one of them to do him good.

decisions.choice: One day; is ... still alive; my friend Jonathan
decisions.reason: Readable sets the scene with "One day", says "still alive" for "left", and reminds the reader who Jonathan was to David. Nothing in the Hebrew marks a new day; it simply begins a new episode.

source.text: וּלְבֵ֨ית שָׁא֥וּל עֶ֨בֶד֙ וּשְׁמ֣וֹ צִיבָ֔א וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ל֖וֹ אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֵלָ֛יו הַאַתָּ֥ה צִיבָ֖א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] house of Saul [belonged] a slave, and his name [was] Ziba, and they called him to David; and said the king to him, [are] you Ziba? And he said, your servant.

en.L: And the house of Saul had a slave, and his name [was] Ziba. And they called him to David, and the king said to him, "[Are] you Ziba?" And he said, "Your servant."
en.B: Now there was a servant of Saul's house named Ziba, and they summoned him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" "I am your servant," he said.
en.R: There was a man named Ziba who had been a servant in Saul's household. He was called to come to David. The king asked him, "Are you Ziba?" "Yes, I am, and I am at your service," he answered.

fr.L: Et la maison de Saül avait un esclave, et son nom [était] Tsiba. Et on l’appela auprès de David, et le roi lui dit : « [Es]-tu Tsiba ? » Et il dit : « Ton serviteur. »
fr.B: Il y avait un serviteur de la maison de Saül nommé Tsiba, et on le fit venir auprès de David. Le roi lui demanda : « Es-tu Tsiba ? » « Je suis ton serviteur », répondit-il.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme appelé Tsiba qui avait été serviteur dans la maison de Saül. On l’a fait venir auprès de David. Le roi lui a demandé : « C’est toi, Tsiba ? » Il a répondu : « Oui, c’est moi, et je suis à ton service. »

decisions.choice: a slave of the house of Saul: a man bound to serve Saul's family
decisions.reason: The word names someone who belongs to a master's household and works under him, not a hired worker. Ziba was bound to Saul's house, yet verses 9-12 show him managing the family's estate with fifteen sons and twenty servants of his own, so he was a senior household servant, a steward, rather than a common laborer.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "yes, I am"
decisions.reason: Speaking to a king, a subject answered with "your servant" instead of "I" (1 Samuel 26:18; 29:8). Ziba both says who he is and puts himself at David's disposal.

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced, Readable); slave (Literal)
decisions.reason: As everywhere, the word is "slave" at Literal and "servant" at Balanced and Readable, so that the bond Ziba lived under is kept without the picture of modern chattel slavery. Ziba's own polite "your servant" is the usual courtesy and is "servant" at every level, as in 1 Samuel.

decisions.choice: Yes, I am, and I am at your service
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both parts of the short reply: he is Ziba, and he is ready to serve the king.

decisions.choice: un esclave (L), un serviteur (B, R) for Ziba; ton serviteur at every level in speech to the king
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch and Samuel terms notes set: "esclave" at Literal for a man bound to a household (m1); "ton serviteur", the subject's polite "I" before the king, is the same at every level.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הַאֶ֨פֶס ע֥וֹד אִישׁ֙ לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה עִמּ֖וֹ חֶ֣סֶד אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ע֛וֹד בֵּ֥ן לִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן נְכֵ֥ה רַגְלָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king, [is there] no longer a man of [the] house of Saul, and I will do with him [the] steadfast love of God? And said Ziba to the king, still [there is] a son of Jonathan, stricken of both feet.

en.L: And the king said, "Is there no longer anyone of the house of Saul, that I may deal [in] the steadfast love of God with him?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, stricken [in] both feet."
en.B: The king asked, "Is there no one left from the house of Saul, to whom I can show the faithful love of God?" Ziba answered the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan. He is lame in both feet."
en.R: The king asked, "Is there not someone left from Saul's family? I want to show him the faithful love that God shows." Ziba answered, "Jonathan has a son who is still alive. Both his feet are crippled."

fr.L: Et le roi dit : « N’y a-t-il plus personne de la maison de Saül, pour que j’agisse envers lui avec l’amour loyal de Dieu ? » Et Tsiba dit au roi : « Il y a encore un fils de Jonathan, infirme des deux pieds. »
fr.B: Le roi demanda : « N’y a-t-il plus personne de la maison de Saül, à qui je puisse montrer l’amour fidèle de Dieu ? » Tsiba répondit au roi : « Il reste encore un fils de Jonathan. Il est infirme des deux pieds. »
fr.R: Le roi a demandé : « Il ne reste personne de la famille de Saül ? Je veux lui montrer un amour fidèle, comme celui que Dieu montre. » Tsiba a répondu : « Jonathan a un fils qui est encore en vie. Il est infirme des deux pieds. »

decisions.choice: the steadfast love of God: love as faithful as God's, promised before God
decisions.reason: The phrase echoes Jonathan's request for "the steadfast love of Yahweh" (1 Samuel 20:14). It points to kindness of the kind God shows, generous and unearned, and to the oath sworn in God's name that binds David to show it.

decisions.choice: stricken in both feet: lame, unable to walk normally
decisions.reason: The word means struck or crippled, and "feet" has the form used for a pair. 4:4 tells how it happened: he was five when news came of Saul's and Jonathan's death, and his nurse dropped him as she fled. Ziba may mention it to show the son is no threat to the throne.

decisions.choice: the faithful love that God shows
decisions.reason: Readable unpacks the short phrase "faithful love of God" into words a young reader can follow, without choosing between the two senses in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵיפֹ֣ה ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּה־ה֗וּא בֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן־עַמִּיאֵ֖ל בְּל֥וֹ דְבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the king, where [is] he? And said Ziba to the king, look, he [is in the] house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.

en.L: And the king said to him, "Where [is] he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he [is in the] house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
en.B: "Where is he?" the king asked him. Ziba said to the king, "He is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
en.R: "Where is he?" the king asked. Ziba answered, "He is staying at the home of Machir son of Ammiel in the town of Lo-debar."

fr.L: Et le roi lui dit : « Où [est]-il ? » Et Tsiba dit au roi : « Voici, il [est dans la] maison de Makir fils d’Ammiel, à Lo-Debar. »
fr.B: « Où est-il ? » lui demanda le roi. Tsiba répondit au roi : « Il est dans la maison de Makir fils d’Ammiel, à Lo-Debar. »
fr.R: « Où est-il ? » a demandé le roi. Tsiba a répondu : « Il habite chez Makir fils d’Ammiel, dans la ville de Lo-Debar. »

decisions.choice: Lo-debar: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Lo-debar lay in Gilead across the Jordan (Joshua 13:26, where the name has a slightly different form), near Mahanaim, where Saul's son Ish-bosheth had ruled (2:8). Machir later brings supplies to David there in his own flight (17:27), so he was a man of standing in that region.

decisions.choice: look: Ziba points to where the son can be found
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what follows; here it is a ready answer: he is right there, at Machir's house.

decisions.choice: look left untranslated
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "look", since the plain answer already carries its sense. Readable adds "staying at" and "the town of" so the reader knows Lo-debar is a place.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִבֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן־עַמִּיאֵ֖ל מִלּ֥וֹ דְבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent King David, and took him from [the] house of Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar.

en.L: And King David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
en.B: So King David sent and had him brought out of the house of Machir son of Ammiel, at Lo-debar.
en.R: So King David sent men to bring him from Machir's house in Lo-debar.

fr.L: Et le roi David envoya et le prit de la maison de Makir fils d’Ammiel, de Lo-Debar.
fr.B: Le roi David l’envoya donc chercher dans la maison de Makir fils d’Ammiel, à Lo-Debar.
fr.R: Alors le roi David a envoyé des hommes le chercher chez Makir, à Lo-Debar.

decisions.choice: sent and took him: had him brought by messengers
decisions.reason: The king is the subject of both verbs, but he acts through the men he sends. The verb "took" does not say whether Mephibosheth came willingly; verse 7 suggests he came in fear.

decisions.choice: had him brought (Balanced); sent men to bring him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that David did not go himself. Readable shortens the repeated names.

source.text: וַ֠יָּבֹא מְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת בֶּן־יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן בֶּן־שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־פָּנָ֖יו וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ מְפִיבֹ֔שֶׁת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul to David, and he fell on his face and bowed down. And said David, Mephibosheth! And he said, here [is] your servant.

en.L: And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came to David, and he fell on his face and bowed down. And David said, "Mephibosheth!" And he said, "Here [is] your servant."
en.B: Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, fell on his face and bowed low. David said, "Mephibosheth!" "I am your servant," he answered.
en.R: When Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son and Saul's grandson, came to David, he bowed down with his face to the ground. David said, "Mephibosheth!" He answered, "Here I am, ready to serve you."

fr.L: Et Mephibosheth fils de Jonathan, fils de Saül, vint auprès de David, et il tomba sur sa face et se prosterna. Et David dit : « Mephibosheth ! » Et il dit : « Voici ton serviteur. »
fr.B: Mephibosheth, fils de Jonathan, fils de Saül, vint auprès de David, tomba sur sa face et se prosterna. David dit : « Mephibosheth ! » « Voici ton serviteur », répondit-il.
fr.R: Quand Mephibosheth, le fils de Jonathan et le petit-fils de Saül, est arrivé devant David, il s’est prosterné, le visage contre le sol. David a dit : « Mephibosheth ! » Il a répondu : « Me voici, à ton service. »

decisions.choice: Mephibosheth: Jonathan's son, also called Merib-baal
decisions.reason: He is named in 4:4. In the lists of Saul's family he is called Merib-baal (1 Chronicles 8:34; 9:40). The name in Samuel probably replaces "baal" with a word meaning "shame", as Ish-bosheth's does, to avoid the name of the god Baal.

decisions.choice: fell on his face and bowed down: full homage to the king
decisions.reason: Lying face down before a king showed submission. For the last living heir of the old royal house, it also showed that he made no claim to the throne and put his life in David's hands.

decisions.choice: here is your servant: I am here, at your service
decisions.reason: The answer to being called by name, as in Genesis 22:1 ("Here I am"), joined with the humble "your servant" used before a superior (verse 2).

decisions.choice: bowed low (Balanced); bowed down with his face to the ground (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both actions in short form. Readable joins them in one picture and says Saul's grandson for "son of Saul" after Jonathan's name.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ דָוִ֜ד אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י עָשֹׂה֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה עִמְּךָ֥ חֶ֨סֶד֙ בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן אָבִ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֣י לְךָ֔ אֶֽת־כָּל־שְׂדֵ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַתָּ֗ה תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם עַל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י תָּמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him David, do not fear, for surely I will do with you steadfast love for [the] sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all [the] field of Saul your father, and you, you will eat bread at my table continually.

en.L: And David said to him, "Do not fear, for I will surely deal [in] steadfast love with you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you yourself will eat bread at my table continually."
en.B: David said to him, "Do not be afraid. I will certainly show you faithful love for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will give you back all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul, and you yourself will always eat at my table."
en.R: David told him, "Do not be afraid. I will be kind to you and show you faithful love, because of your father Jonathan. I will give you back all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. And you will always eat meals with me at my table."

fr.L: Et David lui dit : « Ne crains pas, car j’agirai certainement envers toi avec amour loyal à cause de Jonathan ton père, et je te rendrai tous les champs de Saül ton père, et toi, tu mangeras du pain à ma table continuellement. »
fr.B: David lui dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je vais assurément te montrer un amour fidèle à cause de ton père Jonathan. Je te rendrai toutes les terres de ton grand-père Saül, et toi, tu mangeras toujours à ma table. »
fr.R: David lui a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je serai bon pour toi et je te montrerai un amour fidèle, à cause de ton père Jonathan. Je te rendrai toutes les terres qui appartenaient à ton grand-père Saül. Et tu prendras toujours tes repas avec moi, à ma table. »

decisions.choice: I will surely deal: a firm promise
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled in Hebrew, a way of stressing that the thing will certainly happen. David answers Mephibosheth's fear with a pledge.

decisions.choice: Saul your father: Saul your grandfather
decisions.reason: The word for father also covers a grandfather or any forefather. Saul was Mephibosheth's grandfather (verse 6).

decisions.choice: all the land of Saul: the family's estate
decisions.reason: Saul's family land in Benjamin seems to have passed out of the family's hands after his death, perhaps to the crown. David returns it to Saul's heir, so that the family keeps its inheritance.

decisions.choice: eat bread at my table continually: be provided for by the king as a member of his court
decisions.reason: "Bread" means food or a meal. To eat regularly at the king's table was an honor and a lifelong provision (1 Kings 2:7; 2 Kings 25:29), and it also kept the old royal heir close to the king.

decisions.choice: your grandfather Saul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "grandfather" so the reader does not take Saul to be Mephibosheth's father. Literal keeps "your father".

decisions.choice: I will be kind to you and show you faithful love
decisions.reason: Readable adds "be kind to you" to make plain what David's "faithful love" will mean for this frightened man. It adds no new idea to the Hebrew word.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֕חוּ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פָנִ֔יתָ אֶל־הַכֶּ֥לֶב הַמֵּ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֽוֹנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he bowed down and said, what [is] your servant, that you have turned to the dog, the dead [one], who [is] like me?

en.L: And he bowed down and said, "What [is] your servant, that you have turned to a dead dog such as I?"
en.B: He bowed down again and said, "Who is your servant, that you would pay attention to a dead dog like me?"
en.R: Mephibosheth bowed down again. He said, "Why should you care about me? I am of no more worth than a dead dog."

fr.L: Et il se prosterna et dit : « Qu’[est] ton serviteur, pour que tu te tournes vers un chien mort tel que moi ? »
fr.B: Il se prosterna de nouveau et dit : « Qui est ton serviteur, pour que tu prêtes attention à un chien mort comme moi ? »
fr.R: Mephibosheth s’est prosterné de nouveau. Il a dit : « Pourquoi t’occuper de moi ? Je ne vaux pas plus qu’un chien mort. »

decisions.choice: a dead dog: something utterly worthless
decisions.reason: Dogs in Israel were scavengers, not pets, and a dead dog was the most worthless thing one could name. The phrase was used to belittle oneself before a superior (David to Saul, 1 Samuel 24:15) or to scorn another (16:9). Mephibosheth means that he has nothing to offer the king and deserves no notice.

decisions.choice: you have turned to: you have looked with favor on
decisions.reason: To turn toward someone is to pay attention to them and care for them, as when Yahweh turns to his people (Leviticus 26:9).

decisions.choice: what is your servant: a question that expects the answer "nothing"
decisions.reason: The question is a humble exclamation, not a request for information: he is too lowly for such kindness (compare 7:18).

decisions.choice: a dead dog like me (Balanced); a dead dog such as I (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture, which English readers can follow. Balanced uses "pay attention to" for "turned to"; Literal keeps the verb.

decisions.choice: Why should you care about me? I am of no more worth than a dead dog.
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two and says plainly what the picture means, keeping the dead dog so that the reader still hears Mephibosheth's own words. It names Mephibosheth as the speaker, since the verse begins with only "he".

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶל־צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר שָׁא֖וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה לְשָׁאוּל֙ וּלְכָל־בֵּית֔וֹ נָתַ֖תִּי לְבֶן־אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And called the king to Ziba, [the] servant of Saul, and said to him, all that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to [the] son of your master.

en.L: And the king called Ziba, the attendant of Saul, and said to him, "All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to the son of your master.
en.B: Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's attendant, and said to him, "I have given your master's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and to his whole family.
en.R: Then the king sent for Ziba, who had served Saul. He told him, "I have given Saul's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his family.

fr.L: Et le roi appela Tsiba, le serviteur de Saül, et lui dit : « Tout ce qui appartenait à Saül et à toute sa maison, je l’ai donné au fils de ton maître.
fr.B: Puis le roi fit venir Tsiba, le serviteur de Saül, et lui dit : « J’ai donné au petit-fils de ton maître tout ce qui appartenait à Saül et à toute sa famille.
fr.R: Ensuite le roi a fait venir Tsiba, qui avait servi Saül. Il lui a dit : « J’ai donné au petit-fils de Saül tout ce qui appartenait à Saül et à sa famille.

decisions.choice: attendant: a trusted servant
decisions.reason: The word often means a young man, but it also names a servant or aide of any age, someone who acts for his master (1 Samuel 9:3). Here it describes the same position as "slave of the house of Saul" in verse 2, the steward who looks after the family's affairs.

decisions.choice: the son of your master: Saul's grandson
decisions.reason: "Son" can mean any descendant. The master is Saul; the word has a plural form, a way of showing respect, but means one person. Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson.

decisions.choice: all that belonged to Saul: the royal family's private estate
decisions.reason: This is Saul's family property, not the kingdom. David has already given it back in his promise (verse 7); now he tells the man who manages it, and passes it to Mephibosheth by his word as king.

decisions.choice: attendant (Literal, Balanced); who had served Saul (Readable)
decisions.reason: A different word from the one in verse 2, so Literal and Balanced use "attendant" rather than "servant" or "slave". Readable puts it as a short clause.

decisions.choice: your master's grandson (Balanced); Saul's grandson (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "your master" but says "grandson". Readable names Saul to remove any doubt about which master is meant.

decisions.choice: le serviteur de Saül (L, B)
decisions.reason: A different word from verse 2's (m1): the trusted aide, not the bond-slave. French "serviteur" says this at Literal too, as the English "attendant" does.

source.text: וְעָבַ֣דְתָּ לּ֣וֹ אֶֽת־הָאֲדָמָ֡ה אַתָּה֩ וּבָנֶ֨יךָ וַעֲבָדֶ֜יךָ וְהֵבֵ֗אתָ וְהָיָ֨ה לְבֶן־אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ לֶּ֨חֶם֙ וַאֲכָל֔וֹ וּמְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ יֹאכַ֥ל תָּמִ֛יד לֶ֖חֶם עַל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֑י וּלְצִיבָ֗א חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר בָּנִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will work for him the ground, you and your sons and your slaves, and you will bring in, and it will be for [the] son of your master bread, and he will eat it; and Mephibosheth son of your master will eat continually bread at my table. And to Ziba [were] fifteen sons and twenty slaves.

en.L: And you shall work the ground for him, you and your sons and your slaves, and you shall bring in [the harvest], and it shall be bread for the son of your master, and he shall eat it. But Mephibosheth the son of your master shall eat bread at my table continually." And Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty slaves.
en.B: You, your sons and your servants are to work the land for him and bring in its harvest, to provide food for your master's grandson to eat. But Mephibosheth himself, your master's grandson, will always eat at my table." Ziba had fifteen sons as well as twenty servants.
en.R: You and your sons and your servants must farm the land for him. Bring in the crops, so that his family will have food to eat. But Mephibosheth himself will always eat at my table." Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

fr.L: Et tu travailleras pour lui la terre, toi et tes fils et tes esclaves, et tu rentreras [la récolte], et ce sera du pain pour le fils de ton maître, et il le mangera. Mais Mephibosheth, le fils de ton maître, mangera du pain à ma table continuellement. » Et Tsiba avait quinze fils et vingt esclaves.
fr.B: Toi, tes fils et tes serviteurs, vous cultiverez la terre pour lui et vous en rentrerez la récolte, afin que le petit-fils de ton maître ait de quoi manger. Mais Mephibosheth, le petit-fils de ton maître, mangera toujours à ma table. » Tsiba avait quinze fils et vingt serviteurs.
fr.R: Toi, tes fils et tes serviteurs, vous devrez cultiver la terre pour lui. Rentrez les récoltes, pour que sa famille ait de quoi manger. Mais Mephibosheth lui-même mangera toujours à ma table. » Tsiba avait quinze fils et vingt serviteurs.

decisions.choice: food for your master's grandson, yet he eats at the king's table: the land supports his household
alternatives: the harvest is Mephibosheth's own income, apart from his meals
decisions.reason: The verse says both that the harvest is to feed the son of Ziba's master and that Mephibosheth himself will eat at David's table. The produce most likely supports Mephibosheth's household, his son Mica (verse 12) and those who depend on him, while he himself is fed by the king.

decisions.choice: fifteen sons and twenty slaves: a large household
decisions.reason: Ziba was a man of means in his own right. The numbers show that he could work Saul's estate, and that he had prospered while Saul's heir lived in hiding east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: slaves: workers who belonged to Ziba's household
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 2. Ziba, himself bound to Saul's house, had men bound to serve him.

decisions.choice: bring in [the harvest] (Literal); bring in the harvest (Balanced); bring in the crops (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "bring in"; what is brought in is the produce of the land.

decisions.choice: his family will have food to eat
decisions.reason: Readable states the most likely sense from meaning decision m1, that the produce supports Mephibosheth's household. This is an interpretation of an unclear phrase.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־עַבְדּ֔וֹ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת אֹכֵל֙ עַל־שֻׁלְחָנִ֔י כְּאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Ziba to the king, according to all that commands my lord the king his servant, so will do your servant. And Mephibosheth [is] eating at my table like one of [the] sons of the king.

en.L: And Ziba said to the king, "According to all that my lord the king commands his servant, so will your servant do." [And the king said,] "Mephibosheth [is] eating at my table like one of the sons of the king."
en.B: Ziba said to the king, "Your servant will do everything that my lord the king commands his servant." So the king said, "Mephibosheth will eat at my table like one of the king's sons."
en.R: Ziba answered the king, "Your Majesty, I will do everything you have commanded me." Then the king said, "Mephibosheth will eat at my table, just like one of my own sons."

fr.L: Et Tsiba dit au roi : « Selon tout ce que mon seigneur le roi commande à son serviteur, ainsi fera ton serviteur. » [Et le roi dit :] « Mephibosheth mange à ma table comme l’un des fils du roi. »
fr.B: Tsiba dit au roi : « Ton serviteur fera tout ce que mon seigneur le roi ordonne à son serviteur. » Le roi dit donc : « Mephibosheth mangera à ma table comme l’un des fils du roi. »
fr.R: Tsiba a répondu au roi : « Mon seigneur le roi, je ferai tout ce que tu m’as ordonné. » Alors le roi a dit : « Mephibosheth mangera à ma table, comme un de mes propres fils. »

decisions.choice: at my table: words of the king, following the Hebrew
alternatives: the narrator: "Mephibosheth ate at David's table" (Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "my table", which cannot be Ziba's words. This translation takes the last sentence as David's answer, confirming his order; the Hebrew does not mark a new speaker, so this is a reading of a hard phrase. The ancient Greek translation reads "David's table", which makes the sentence the narrator's statement: "So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons". The sense is the same in each case: Mephibosheth is treated like a royal son.

decisions.choice: my lord the king ... his servant ... your servant: court courtesy
decisions.reason: Ziba speaks of the king and of himself in the third person, the respectful way to address a king. He promises full obedience.

decisions.choice: like one of the king's sons: given the place of a son
decisions.reason: The heir of the rival royal house is treated as a member of David's own family. The kindness David swore to Jonathan (1 Samuel 20:15, 42) is kept beyond what was asked.

decisions.choice: [And the king said,] (Literal); So the king said (Balanced); Then the king said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Words supplied to show the speaker, following the reading in meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty, I will do everything you have commanded me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the third-person courtesy into plain first and second person and keeps the respect with "Your Majesty".

source.text: וְלִמְפִיבֹ֥שֶׁת בֵּן־קָטָ֖ן וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מִיכָ֑א וְכֹל֙ מוֹשַׁ֣ב בֵּית־צִיבָ֔א עֲבָדִ֖ים לִמְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Mephibosheth [was] a young son, and his name [was] Mica; and every dweller of [the] house of Ziba [were] servants to Mephibosheth.

en.L: And Mephibosheth had a young son, and his name [was] Mica. And all who lived in the house of Ziba [were] servants to Mephibosheth.
en.B: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. Everyone who lived in Ziba's household became servants of Mephibosheth.
en.R: Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. All the people in Ziba's household worked for Mephibosheth.

fr.L: Et Mephibosheth avait un jeune fils, et son nom [était] Mika. Et tous ceux qui habitaient la maison de Tsiba [étaient] serviteurs de Mephibosheth.
fr.B: Mephibosheth avait un jeune fils nommé Mika. Tous ceux qui habitaient dans la maison de Tsiba devinrent serviteurs de Mephibosheth.
fr.R: Mephibosheth avait un jeune fils qui s’appelait Mika. Tous les gens de la maison de Tsiba travaillaient pour Mephibosheth.

decisions.choice: Mica: Saul's line continues
decisions.reason: Mica (spelled Micah in 1 Chronicles 8:34-35; 9:40-41) carried on the family of Jonathan, whose descendants are listed there for many generations. David's kindness kept Saul's line alive.

decisions.choice: servants to Mephibosheth: bound to serve him
decisions.reason: Here the word describes the service the whole of Ziba's household now owed Mephibosheth, his own sons included, rather than whether each person was owned.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "servants" here rather than "slaves", because the sentence speaks of a duty to serve laid on a whole household, Ziba's free sons among them.

source.text: וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת יֹשֵׁב֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י עַל־שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ תָּמִ֖יד ה֣וּא אֹכֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא פִסֵּ֖חַ שְׁתֵּ֥י רַגְלָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Mephibosheth [was] dwelling in Jerusalem, for at [the] table of the king continually he [was] eating; and he [was] lame [in] both his feet.

en.L: And Mephibosheth was living in Jerusalem, for he ate at the table of the king continually. And he [was] lame [in] both his feet.
en.B: So Mephibosheth made his home in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king's table. He was lame in both feet.
en.R: Mephibosheth stayed in Jerusalem, because he ate at the king's table every day. Both his feet were crippled.

fr.L: Et Mephibosheth habitait à Jérusalem, car il mangeait à la table du roi continuellement. Et il [était] boiteux des deux pieds.
fr.B: Mephibosheth s’établit donc à Jérusalem, car il mangeait toujours à la table du roi. Il était boiteux des deux pieds.
fr.R: Mephibosheth est resté à Jérusalem, parce qu’il mangeait tous les jours à la table du roi. Il était infirme des deux pieds.

decisions.choice: was living ... ate: an ongoing way of life
decisions.reason: Both verbs are participles that describe a lasting state. Mephibosheth's home was now in Jerusalem, near the king, rather than on the family land, which Ziba worked for him.

decisions.choice: lame in both his feet: the chapter ends where Ziba began
decisions.reason: The chapter closes as verse 3 opened, with his disability. The kindness he receives does not depend on his worth or strength, and his lameness will matter again in his story (19:27).

decisions.choice: Both of his feet were crippled
decisions.reason: Readable uses the same plain wording as in verse 3.
